comparisons.peer_topic: Stock Repurchase Program Activity and Status
comparisons.peer_summary: AMD's authorized $12 billion stock repurchase program saw the company repurchase 5.9 million shares for $862 million during the fiscal year ended December 28, 2024, with $4.7 billion remaining as of that date. The program has no termination date and may be suspended or discontinued at any time without obligation to acquire any specific amount of stock.
comparisons.comparison: Both MU and AMD disclose their 2024 stock repurchase activity, authorized amounts, and program terms under Item 8. MU repurchased 3.2 million shares for $300 million in 2024 against a $10 billion authorization with no expiration date, while AMD repurchased 5.9 million shares for $862 million against a $12 billion authorization, also with no termination date. Both companies state their programs do not obligate them to acquire any specific amount of stock.

sentences.text: Our Board of Directors has authorized the discretionary repurchase of up to $10 billion of our outstanding common stock through open-market purchases, block trades, privately-negotiated transactions, derivative transactions, and/or pursuant to Rule 10b5-1 trading plans.

The repurchase authorization has no expiration date, does not obligate us to acquire any common stock, and is subject to market conditions and our ongoing determination of the best use of available cash.
We repurchased 3.2 million shares of our common stock for $300 million in 2024 and 8.6 million shares for $425 million in 2023.
The Company has an approved stock repurchase program authorizing repurchases of up to $12 billion of the Company's common stock (Repurchase Program).
During the year ended December 28, 2024, the Company repurchased 5.9 million shares of its common stock under the Repurchase Program for $862 million.
This Repurchase Program does not obligate the Company to acquire any common stock, has no termination date and may be suspended or discontinued at any time.

comparisons.peer_summary: Broadcom utilized all $20 billion of authorized stock repurchase amounts (originally authorized in December 2021 and May 2022) prior to their expiration on December 31, 2023. In fiscal year 2024, the company repurchased and retired approximately 67 million shares for $7,176 million.
comparisons.comparison: Both MU and AVGO report on significant stock repurchase activity in fiscal year 2024. MU repurchased $300 million worth of shares in 2024 under a $10 billion ongoing authorization. In contrast, AVGO repurchased $7,176 million in 2024 but noted that its prior $20 billion authorized programs were fully utilized and expired on December 31, 2023, with no new ongoing authorization disclosed for 2024 in the same manner as MU's. AVGO's activity reflects the completion of older programs, whereas MU's reflects ongoing capacity.

sentences.text: We repurchased 3.2 million shares of our common stock for $300 million in 2024 and 8.6 million shares for $425 million in 2023.
Through August 29, 2024, we had repurchased an aggregate of $7.19 billion under the authorization.

All $20 billion of the authorized amount under these stock repurchase programs was utilized prior to expiration on December 31, 2023.

comparisons.comparison: The target disclosure (MU) concerns common stock repurchases (buybacks), while the Intels (INTC) candidate concerns Employee Stock Purchase Plans (ESPP). Although both involve the issuance/acquisition of common stock and capital resources, they are distinct financial activities: repurchases reduce outstanding shares via company buybacks, while ESPPs involve employee purchases. The topics are related under equity transactions but not substantively comparable as share repurchase programs.

comparisons.peer_topic: Share Repurchase Program Authorization and Activity
comparisons.peer_summary: In August 2023, the Board authorized an additional $25.0 billion for share repurchases without expiration, with $9.7 billion spent in fiscal 2024 and $1.9 billion in early 2024. As of January 28, 2024, $22.5 billion remained authorized, and the program aims to offset employee dilution while remaining subject to market conditions.
comparisons.comparison: Both MU and NVDA disclose active share repurchase programs with specific authorization amounts and 2024 activity. MU has a $10 billion authorization with no expiration and repurchased $300 million in 2024. NVDA has a $22.5 billion remaining authorization (following a $25 billion increase) and repurchased $9.7 billion in fiscal 2024, plus an additional $1.9 billion in early 2024. Both programs are subject to market conditions and aim to manage capital allocation, with NVDA explicitly noting the intent to offset employee dilution.
